claims.title: Exact conditional sampling from a bounded-energy Gaussian source has a sharp copy optimum
claims.claim: For each integer s>=1, h=4s^2, let B0=[[1/4,0],[0,0]] and B1=[[1/4,1/(4s)],[1/(4s),0]] define normalized pure Gaussian states. Both formulas are known but label i is hidden. For independent unconditional copies, an always-output procedure realizing exactly the second-mode count law conditional on first-mode count h for either source has minimum fixed budget N*=ceil(log Z_h/(-log F_h)), where A_j=product_{r=0}^{j-1}(1-2r/h)^2, Z_h=sum_{j=0}^{h/2} A_j/(2j)!, and F_h=sqrt(1-(8h-1)/(15h^2)) is the SQUARED pure-state overlap. N*/h -> (15/4)log(cosh 1)=1.626678... . P0=delta_0; P1(2j)=A_j/((2j)!Z_h).
claims.interface: Unknown label; copies are the only source-dependent resource. Arbitrary collective/adaptive measurements are allowed; label-bearing advice, preparation-unitary access and conditional-state oracles are excluded. Output law is assessed unconditionally, charging failures. TV(P,Q)=1/2 sum|P-Q| and quantum trace distance=1/2||rho-sigma||_1. Integer h is restricted to 4s^2.
claims.proof_spine: The zero-output effect must fix source 0, forcing F_h^N<=1/Z_h. Vacuum/nonvacuum detection in mode 2 has no-click probability F_h^N under source 1; rebalancing positive output mass attains the criterion. Integer boundaries reduce to the rational inequality [1-(8h-1)/(15h^2)]^N Z_h^2<=1. Geometric proposals for the known positive law use rational acceptance 2^J A_J/(2J)!.
claims.costs: Unconditional input mean photon count <=1/4; conditional output mean <=sinh(1). With label supplied, exact sampling uses <=4/3 expected proposals and expected bit work polynomial in log h. Exact acquisition rebalancing setup is polynomial in h, with O(h log h)-bit operands; copy optimality is not classical-runtime optimality. At TV<=1/12 fixed copies need N>=5h/96; almost-sure termination with adaptive count needs max_i E_i T>=5h/9216. Exact fair-bit algorithms have no bounded worst-case random-bit claim.
claims.failure: One heralded attempt can use one copy; its success probability cannot be discarded. The fixed-budget exact optimum does not apply to expected-copy budgets or arbitrary devices without this promise. Sufficiency assumes ideal independent preparations and ideal vacuum detection. No quantum hardware or physical acquisition was demonstrated.
claims.comparator: Two-state quantum discrimination/fidelity mechanisms are established prior art. The exact Gaussian operational witness and complete interface have unresolved historical priority.
claims.gate: Obtain independent expert or formal review of the exact fixed-copy criterion, algebraic rebalancing coin and expected-bit sampler; determine priority of the exact witness without claiming novelty of discrimination.
claims.related_scope: Acquisition boundary for supplied-model conditional computation; does not refute either earlier supplied-model theorem.

claims.title: A supplied positive Gaussian single-herald compiler extends to nonnegative displacement
claims.claim: For an explicitly supplied rational symmetric entrywise nonnegative 2m-by-2m Bargmann kernel K, nonnegative rational displacement ell, ket/bra exchange symmetry, rho(XK)<1, one nonzero-probability herald h encoded in binary, and error epsilon, the internal construction samples remaining physical counts to TV<=epsilon in bit work polynomial in complete input length, m, log(h+1), log(1/epsilon), with certified polynomial-time elementary evaluations. Physicality of the density operator is an additional supplied promise. Uniform complexity of the particular Python/Arb refinement implementation remains unproved.
claims.interface: One physical herald, binary output counts, rational nonnegative K and ell, normalizability and physicality. X exchanges ket/bra blocks. No arbitrary complex/signed kernels or multiple herald modes. Supplied exact parameters are not acquired from a device. The zero-displacement baseline and displaced extension have distinct endpoint/error allocations.
claims.proof_spine: Schur elimination leaves [[a,b],[b,a]] with singleton weights (c,c). Cross-count weights w(k)=b^k H_(h-k)(a,c)^2/k!, H_n=[z^n]exp(a z^2/2+c z). Each parity subsequence is log-concave, though the full law need not be. Approximate ratio anchors plus factor-two inflation combine two envelopes without parity normalizers, total envelope mass <=12 times target mass. Conditional own-pair laws have decreasing ratios. Source Poisson and aggregate reverse-Schur binomial/negative-binomial draws reconstruct counts; N537 supplies coefficient evaluation.
claims.costs: No enumeration of h photons. Graph/routing operations and scalar-call bound O(m^3); rational pivot and large-count bit lengths, precision, capped tickets, rejection/fallback events and TV budget are charged. Final displaced endpoint allocates epsilon/4 to tickets and 3epsilon/4 across at most max_scalar_calls+4 scalar draws. Source reports undisplaced h=10^100 and displaced h=10^20 runs; these are finite observations, not uniform runtime or fastest-software evidence.
claims.failure: Full-law unimodality is refuted at h=2,a=1/4,b=7/40,c=1/100; parity splitting bypasses this failure without making that counterexample obsolete. Earlier displaced_gate.txt says no route had then been established; final followup establishes an internal constructive route. Only repaired endpoint APIs have the audited integer/ticket contract. Historical broad software tests precede final narrow evaluator repairs; final hashes and targeted regressions must be read together. No physical preparation/calibration, finite-sample verification of tiny TV error, formal or external validation is supplied.
claims.comparator: Extends Astra N417/N418 at a scoped supplied-model interface. Gaussian moments, trinomial bridges, generic log-concave rejection and loop/path representations have prior art; complete compiler priority is UNKNOWN.
claims.gate: Close the uniform precision-refinement runtime gap for the actual numerical endpoint and independently review the full encoded TV contract and final-code audit lineage.
claims.related_scope: Source-reported extension and endpoint audits of positive single-herald supplied-model sampling; original claims/statuses remain intact.

claims.title: Positive parity-folded Gaussian moments admit binary-index logarithmic coefficient evaluation
claims.claim: For all rational a,c>=0, binary integer n>=0, p>=1, H_n=[z^n]exp(a z^2/2+c z) can be recognized as zero or log H_n enclosed with absolute width <=2^-p in deterministic bit work polynomial in rational input length, log(n+1), and p. An expanded exact rational coefficient is not promised; it may require Omega(n) bits.
claims.interface: Nonnegative rational coefficients and a logarithmic interval/scaled mantissa-exponent output; exact zeros and elementary a=0 or c=0 cases handled separately. The mathematical algorithm and the actual adaptive Arb implementation have distinct complexity statuses. Symbols a,c,n and center u below are local.
claims.proof_spine: For a,c>0, d=c/sqrt(a), sigma=(-1)^n, u=(d+sqrt(d^2+4n))/2: H_n=a^(n/2)/(n!sqrt(2pi)) integral_0^infinity t^n exp(-(t-d)^2/2)[1+sigma exp(-2dt)]dt. Fold parity before approximation; odd factor uses -expm1(-2dt). Normalize at u, use a uniform positive integral lower bound, Gaussian tails, and bounded complex extension. Certified Taylor quadrature or independently justified rational interpolation gives polynomial precision/cost. Use u-d=n/u to control cancellation in log prefactors. Small n uses a short positive finite sum.
claims.costs: For retained radius R=O(sqrt(p)), rational panels width 1/2 and q+1 equally spaced nodes give pointwise error <=(128/3)(2/3)^(q+1), total weight <=2R(2e)^q; q=O(p+log R), polynomial guard precision. Cancellation in prefactors needs O(log n) extra precision. Does not promise a polynomial-sized expanded coefficient or uniform runtime of a particular library.
claims.failure: Signed saddle subtraction can lose tiny odd displacement; the positive folding route avoids that obstruction. Relative error for H_n and absolute width for log H_n need explicit precision conversion; they are not the same quantity. Source code/audits remain ordinary model-assisted numerical evidence, not formal/expert certification.
claims.comparator: Gaussian moments/Hermite and parabolic-cylinder quantities and the integral identity are classical. Originality of the uniform complete encoded interface remains UNKNOWN.
claims.gate: Independently certify uniform analytic/bit-cost bounds and audit the implemented Taylor recurrence, guard precision and final domain repairs; resolve prior art for the encoded evaluation contract.
claims.related_scope: Reusable coefficient interface; no automatic application to signed or complex coefficients.

claims.title: Atomic signals can absorb fixed positive semicircular noise with exponentially close full spectral laws
aliases: atomic signal noise deconvolution full law
claims.claim: For a,b>0 and k>=1, let mu_k=sum_j p_j delta_(x_j), x_j=2sqrt(a)cos(j pi/(k+1)), p_j=2sin^2(j pi/(k+1))/(k+1). Under the stated IID exact-draw model, nu_0=SC_(a+b) and nu_1=mu_k free-convolved SC_b have noise variances differing by a while their entire laws have TV<=min(1,R H_k(r)/pi), whenever rho=sqrt(a/(a+b))<r<1 and rho+3sqrt(D_k(r))<r. Here R=2sqrt(a)+2sqrt(b), D_k(r)=(b/(a+b))r^(2k+2)(1+r^2)/(1-r^(2k+2)), H_k(r)=3sqrt(D_k(r))/sqrt(a)+E_k(r), E_k(r)=r^(2k+1)(1+r^2)/(sqrt(a)(1-r^(2k+2))). At fixed a,b,r the bound is O(r^k). For a=b=1,k=100 the source proves TV<=8.121e-13 and more than 8.535e11 IID exact-law samples are needed for its variance-estimation guarantee; 850 billion are insufficient.
claims.interface: Observe IID exact real draws from nu=mu free-convolved SC_t. Unknown mu has at most k positive-weight real atoms in a supplied compact interval; t>0 is unknown. The claim does not concern the joint eigenvalue law of a finite matrix. Unlimited computation and knowledge that the hidden input is the displayed pair are allowed; the exact atom count is not supplied.
claims.proof_spine: Chebyshev quadrature gives a rational resolvent identity for the explicit atoms. A two-root disk argument continues the physical free-subordination root, including at spectral edges, to bound the Cauchy-transform gap. Uniform density bounds turn the transform estimate into full-law TV on compact support. Two-point testing and product coupling give the sample lower bound; an exact rational certificate checks the k=100 constant.
claims.costs: The pair uses O(k) atoms and storage. At k=100 the analytical TV bound is 8.121e-13 and the source lower bound exceeds 8.535e11 IID law samples for the stated error/success guarantee. This is an information lower bound, not computation time or samples physically collected.
claims.failure: Does not cover correlated eigenvalues of one finite random matrix, full matrix entries or a physical instrument. At zero lower noise the displayed known pair is separated by discrete-versus-continuous support; repeated shared-signal noisy matrices change the access model. Neither escape is free under an unstated resource contract.
claims.comparator: Astra N526 concerns Pick feasibility for its known-atomic-model interface. This full-law IID result is a scoped continuation, not an invalidation or status correction. Free deconvolution, quadrature and two-point testing have prior art.

claims.status_boundary: Source-reported internally reconstructed proof, adversarial model criticism and finite checks; no external/formal certification, historical priority or empirical acquisition is established. The model is IID draws from a limiting spectral law, not correlated eigenvalues of one matrix.

claims.title: Exact low-order marginals can leave rare-event probability uncertain at the rare-event scale
aliases: bounded coordinate assay transcript lower bound
claims.claim: Let P0=Bern(a)^d with 0<a<=1/2, target A={1}, p=a^d and integer 0<=k<d. Set D_k=sum_(j=0)^k binom(d,j)((1-a)/a)^j and K=p^-1-D_k. If D_k<=K, the source constructs nonnegative P* with every marginal on at most k coordinates exactly equal to P0, P*(A)=2p and chi-square(P*||P0)=1/K<=2p. This divergence is minimal among laws satisfying those marginal and event-mass constraints. An adaptive assay revealing at most k distinct coordinates from each fresh specimen has identical transcript laws under P0 and P*, even with unlimited specimens. A separate positive regime assumes known product structure and explicit polynomial-size DNF failure modes and composes established product-estimation/weighted-witness methods.
claims.interface: Known d,a,k and a rare conjunction under a Bernoulli product baseline. The negative pair is indistinguishable from supplied low-order marginals; the assay reveals at most k distinct coordinates per fresh specimen. Reusing a specimen to observe more coordinates changes the contract. The positive regime requires true product structure and explicit DNF representation.
claims.proof_spine: In L^2(P0), split the point-evaluation reproducing kernel at the all-ones vector into degrees <=k and >k. The high-degree residual is orthogonal to every function of <=k coordinates. Adding it to the likelihood ratio doubles target-event mass while preserving all those marginals. Its squared norm gives the chi-square value; Cauchy-Schwarz proves optimality. Transcript coupling handles the stated adaptive fresh-specimen assay.
claims.costs: The source gives a full-vector relative-estimation lower bound of Omega(1/(epsilon^2 p)) under its stated conditions despite exact supplied marginals through order k. P* has a compact exact rejection sampler with reported acceptance 1/2; constructing it does not reveal which real-world law holds. The positive product/DNF regime charges measurements and arithmetic and uses known methods.
claims.failure: D_k<=K is required. The divergence optimum is not by itself a finite-sample minimax theorem for every assay. Product and explicit-DNF assumptions are essential to the positive regime. No real failure law or general rare-event capability is established.
claims.comparator: Astra N492 studies rare-event certificate acquisition under a different interface. This result supplies a moment-matching/k-coordinate construction; it does not imply all higher-order validation is impossible.
claims.gate: Independently verify the reproducing-kernel optimality and adaptive-transcript quantifiers; price any escape through extra coordinates, specimen reuse, structure acquisition or conditional-law access.
claims.related_scope: Complementary rare-event acquisition obstruction with a distinct marginal/assay interface; no invalidation of N492.
claims.status_boundary: Source-reported internal proof reconstruction, model criticism, exact checks and synthetic comparator. External/formal validation, priority and empirical law identification are not established.
claims.unavailable: External correctness and novelty UNKNOWN; no finite-sample minimax claim beyond the displayed constructions.

claims.title: A restricted low-energy Gaussian conditional sampler is polynomially equivalent to perfect-matching approximation
aliases: Gaussian conditional sampling perfect matching FPRAS
claims.claim: For the explicitly constructed rational, nonnegative, pure undisplaced Gaussian pair kernels with operator norm<1/2 and mean photon number<5/12, condition on one photon in every graph mode and leave two output modes unheralded. A classical conditional sampler with adjustable TV error and polynomial runtime in exact input length and inverse error is polynomially equivalent, under the stated reductions, to an FPRAS for perfect matchings of arbitrary unweighted simple graphs, including exact zero detection.
claims.interface: Restricted supplied Gaussian family and graph; one unit-photon herald in every original graph mode, two output modes remain. The sampler must work uniformly over every nonzero herald. The reductions charge precision, encoded bit length, conditional calls, zero heralds and sample budget.
claims.proof_spine: Attach two leaves to an edge uv. The two remaining modes output only 00 or 11 with q=R^2 p_uv^2/(1+R^2 p_uv^2), where p_uv is a uniform-perfect-matching edge marginal. Dyadic calibration and self-reduction recover the count from conditional samples; approximate counting supplies the reverse direction. Source replays check finite graph/hafnian identities and support.
claims.costs: The reduction uses O(n^2 log(n/delta)+n^3 epsilon^-2 log(n/delta)) conditional samples plus a coarse-search term; the finest requested TV error is Theta(epsilon/n). Literal herald rejection costs at least (63/128)4^n preparations per accepted calibrated event. The direct sampler is not implemented; proof constants request about 7.3e8 samples already at n=2, epsilon=.1, delta=.01.
claims.failure: This is an equivalence, not an efficient conditional sampler, matching algorithm or complexity separation. It applies only to the stated family and herald pattern. Variable-subset GBS has a different output law and does not supply the required conditional guarantee.
claims.comparator: Astra N417/N419 cover Gaussian samplers/reductions at distinct interfaces. Hafnian graph encodings and variable-subset GBS are prior art; this result does not claim the broad Gaussian/matching connection as new.
claims.gate: Find a proved direct conditional sampler or a materially different resource contract; otherwise obtain expert review of both reduction directions and retain the capability barrier.
claims.related_scope: Restricted family/unit-herald equivalence; existing sampler cards keep their original interfaces and statuses.
claims.status_boundary: Source-reported reconstructed reductions, adversarial model criticism and exact finite checks. External/formal correctness, novelty, an implemented conditional sampler and physical acquisition are not established.
claims.unavailable: The required sampler, practical matching capability, external correctness and historical priority remain unestablished.

claims.title: A delayed division-noise model matches one growth summary but predicts a conflicting age-variance trend
claims.claim: Under a fixed-period model with independent mean-zero division innovations, the report derives conditional within/across-division MSD formulas and an explicit causal delayed response h_l(t)=h_0(t-l). Numerically choosing l≈1.301 hours makes one defined continuous-lag aggregate ratio R=1/2 for T=10.2 hours and chosen integral memory 5.4 hours. The model also predicts suppressed short-lag changes across division, quiet within-cycle intervals and an upturn in growth averaged since birth late in the cycle. Synthetic measurements reportedly separate its first prediction from an OU comparator; a published age-variance curve is qualitatively in tension with the upturn. This is a falsification-oriented countermodel, not a biological explanation.
claims.interface: Centered log-growth fluctuation is driven only by independent division innovations through a specified continuous causal pulse. T=10.2 hours and integral memory 5.4 hours are chosen values, not measured parameters. Synthetic filtering uses the author's Matérn-3/2 covariance implementation, not the full experimental Julia pipeline. No raw experimental trajectory was acquired or reanalysed.
claims.proof_spine: Exact phase identities give constant age variance and phase-averaged covariance for an inherited sine/plateau/cosine pulse. A time shift preserves those identities while changing alignment with division. Conditional MSD integrals yield a delayed-response root for one chosen aggregate statistic. Synthetic filtering tests further predictions, including a raw-log-mass second-difference covariance diagnostic; a late-cycle variance formula yields the qualitative published-curve tension.
claims.costs: Reported internal checks compare adaptive quadrature with closed forms and state-space outputs with dense calculations. Synthetic trials use 24 lineages by 10 cycles per condition and reused seeds; these are not empirical replications. Raw-data estimation, the full experimental pipeline, causal perturbation and molecular mechanism acquisition are absent. The specific analysis scripts/environment named in the report were not attached.
claims.failure: The delay matches a theoretical null and was not fitted to raw trajectories. The apparent age-variance mismatch is a qualitative warning, not formal rejection, because source trajectories and processing were not replayed. The response has no measured molecular source. A reported matrix builder reads uninitialized storage; Julia was unavailable. Glass and peroxide work was screened, not explained.
claims.comparator: A continuation of Astra N494/N496/N499 pulse and provenance work. This report does not validate or correct those historical claims. The cited 2026 growth-noise preprint was not fully reviewed; priority is UNKNOWN.
claims.gate: Obtain the cited code/environment and raw data; independently reproduce the full pipeline on held-out cycles with trend, lineage and selection controls; then perturb the proposed delay without refitting. No biological mechanism should be inferred before these observations.
claims.related_scope: A delayed-response continuation of inherited pulse/provenance records; no raw-data confirmation or change in earlier status.
claims.status_boundary: Attached natural-sciences record reports conditional formulas, synthetic diagnostics and a falsification-oriented countermodel. It explicitly establishes no raw-data result, molecular mechanism, independent correctness or historic breakthrough.
claims.unavailable: Raw trajectories, analysis scripts/environment, Julia execution and independent scientific review were not supplied. Biological causality, superiority and historical novelty remain UNKNOWN.
